answer.evidence: The main body is the bench (rows 12-46, width 78). Rows 13-18 are a brown top plane that ends in a light front-edge line at row 19, with a lighter row 20 and a dark shadow row 21. Below it the front face runs rows 22-45, about 24 rows, with panels and a coin emblem. The three chair backs (rows 0-11, width 30 each) are flat vertical faces with no seat visible, because the bench hides the seats. So the object reads as a bench with a proper top, not as a seat whose seat surface is seen from above. The chairs' own horizontal surfaces are missing.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate's dark edge pixels are 100% near-neutral, so the outline is a near-black line around the bench and chairs, not a dark tone of the adjacent wood. This is the sticker look; the references with tinted outlines (hedge, stall, well) avoid it. Flat-fill coverage is 31%, against 0-13% for the references. The wooden front panel is a large area of mostly one brown with only faint grain and a few plank lines. The chair backs are small dark blocks with 2-3 steps. Only 16 distinct colours, against 38-40 for the stall and well. The median of 7 colours per tile is below the richest references (17-20) and below the hedge (10). The wood ramp has about 3 steps, against 5-6 in the references. The composition and the coin emblem read clearly, but the shading is shallow and flat next to the Beodeul pieces.
